explanation: Virtual method with override uses dynamic dispatch; actual type is Derived, so Derived.Print() is called.
Auto-property with object initializer sets X to 5 via the setter.
Base constructor runs first implicitly, then derived; outputs A then B.
Generic class Box<int> stores int values; Value is set to 42 via object initializer.
Abstract method must be overridden in derived class; Circle.Draw() prints "Circle".
Interface method is implemented; calling Get() via interface reference executes the implementation.
Static class contains static methods callable without instantiation; 3 + 4 = 7.
Property X has private backing field x with read-only getter; X returns 10.
Static field Count is shared across all instances; incremented twice by two constructor calls.
Method overloading: M(int) matches the argument type, so B is printed.
